note: Italian style, by L. B. Dixon. Lot 193 ft on Prairie Avenue by 175 ft to the alley; the house's extreme size 66 ft 6 in on Prairie Avenue by 94 ft deep. A basement faced with Portland brownstone ashlar, rubbed, with square rustic joints, 6 ft high with a moulded base and water-table, its windows entirely above ground; Baltimore pressed brick above; every window trimmed with brownstone. An east front; the main entrance through a tower 73 ft high, up stone steps covered by a stone porch on fluted Corinthian columns; the reception room south of the hall with a half-octagonal stone bay to the south and two front windows under a stone verandah on fluted Corinthian columns, whose roof is a balcony with a stone balustrade; the parlor north of it with two front windows opening on a stone balcony on brackets; an octagonal library behind it; the dining room with two south windows and a side entrance on the south. Storeys: basement 9 ft, principal 14 ft 9 in, second 13 ft 6 in; the main floor 6 ft over grade; the main building 44 ft to the top of its cornice, the rear part 37 ft; an attic lit by frieze-light windows; slate roof with copper flashings. The barn 39 by 80 ft, of the same materials.
